answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a refundable bond before accepting orders, whether it sells a fable, nectar, or quartz. The bond stays locked through a dispute window and is slashed when an adjudicator verifies fraud. Creating fresh identities does not bypass this requirement: an attacker running 1,000 sellers must fund 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and risking its loss on each fraudulent account.
